missing_across_line.topic: Core's battery compartment as a drop-safe and fire-safe enclosure: UL 153 Supplement SA's drop programme and the acrylic around the cells
missing_across_line.products: Core, including the Core ball, which is sold separately
missing_across_line.why_it_matters: DOCUMENTED: Core's listing route is UL 153 with Supplement SA (r32-lamps-final:spinoffs/barkhorn/companions/launch/certification.md; PARTICULARS.md). UL says SA has 'a more demanding drop impact test program than historically applied to other portable luminaires', aligned with ANSI/PLATO FL-1. FL-1's impact test is at least 1 m onto concrete, in six orientations. SA also limits battery power to cut fire risk (https://www.ul.com/news/ul-153-expanded-add-battery-operated-portable-luminaires; https://www.streamlight.com/resources/learning/ansi-information). Core's test plan (.../launch/first-articles.md) covers runtime, charge heat, NTC cut-outs, wrong or reversed cells, IPX4, an 8 deg incline and touch. It has no drop test, no external short or cell-vent case, and no check of the enclosure material. WHAT WOULD FACE THE DROP (.../companions/crystal.py:398-421; PARTICULARS.md): three cells, the board and the LED sit inside a turned black cast-acrylic drum, 120 x 30. About 2 mm of acrylic separates the cell bays from the ball's cup (lamps review). Below is a 2.3 mm aluminium hatch. On top, loose on a silicone seat, is a 0.76 kg hollow ball made of two formed halves 'joined at the equator'. The reviews' own numbers make falls routine: 4.5 N at the top tips the lamp, and the ball rolls out at 38.7 deg or 6.0 N. The bar plan puts 'a Core lamp on every table' (r33-planet-world:spinoffs/barkhorn/planet/README.md:208). From 1 m that is 1.46 x 9.81 x 1.0 = 14 J for the lamp, or 0.76 x 9.81 = 7.5 J for a loose ball, landing on a notch-brittle material. Nobody has an estimate or a coupon test. FIRE: standard cast PMMA is recognised only to UL 94 HB (e.g. Evonik ACRYLITE, https://www.ledil.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/UL_ACRYLITE.pdf). The only UL 94 question on file (r46-owner-notes:spinoffs/barkhorn/research/2026-10-31/R3-compliance.md, open item 5) names Hemisphere's diffusers and Tropos's cabinet, not Core. Core's 14.4 Wh 1S3P pack could drive up to 3.2 V / (0.038 ohm / 3) = 250 A into a fault inside the drum (datasheet <=38 mOhm, an upper bound). Above it sits about 19 MJ of PMMA (0.76 kg x ~25 MJ/kg, my estimate). SA's numeric battery limit is still R3's open item 2. CORE-RECHARGE.md's v1 'Option 1' would put a ~19 Wh Li-ion (NMC) pack in the same base. Its case for LiFePO4, that it 'sees no thermal runaway at these sizes', overstates it: LFP runs away at a higher temperature, but it can still run away. TIMING: the ball mould is ordered 16 Nov and the halves joined 4 Jan (first-articles.md). Nothing drops or abuses a unit before tooling, so a failure would surface at the lab after the moulds are cut. NEEDED NOW: SA's exact drop and battery clauses from the lab; drop tests on formed-ball, equator-joint and 2 mm-web coupons; and a metal or V-rated barrier around the bays, or the lab's written acceptance of HB.

missing_across_line.topic: Chemical compatibility and stress cracking beyond the cleaning card: thread-locker on stressed acrylic, bar spirits and sanitisers, and cement vapour sealed into cemented cavities
missing_across_line.products: Hemisphere, Core, Mantle (Tropos already has a control)
missing_across_line.why_it_matters: DOCUMENTED FOR TROPOS ONLY: crazing is risk A1 in r33-speaker-horn:spinoffs/barkhorn/make/horn-risks.md. The README (r33-speaker-horn:spinoffs/barkhorn/README.md:320) requires 'no crazing at the inserts and the joints after a 48-hour solvent-wipe test (isopropanol) on an annealed shot', and FAI V4 checks stress in polarised light. The lamps and Mantle have no compatibility list and no test, and four live specifications put stress-cracking agents on stressed acrylic. (1) Hemisphere's clamp ring screws onto the collar's M96 x 1.5 thread over the clamped formed crown that hangs the shade overhead, with 'a drop of thread-lock' (r32-lamps-final:spinoffs/barkhorn/companions/crystal.py:226-233). Anaerobic lockers are methacrylate esters. Henkel's Loctite 243 data sheet says it is 'not normally recommended for use on plastics (particularly thermoplastic materials where stress cracking of the plastic could result)' (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/24239.pdf). The thread sits directly above the crown, so excess locker runs onto acrylic held under clamp preload, at the overhead load path. (2) The Mantle reviewer's own fix, 'torque to about 0.3 N m with thread-locker', would put the same chemistry under the six M4 heads that already bear on the platter at 13-42 MPa. (3) The bar plan puts a Core on every table, 15 in all (r33-planet-world:spinoffs/barkhorn/planet/README.md:208; r42/NUMBERS.md:53). The same project's brief says 'spirits craze acrylic' (planet/BRIEF.md:25), the care copy bans alcohol (r47-brand:spinoffs/barkhorn/press/core.md:15), and the lamps review found no anneal step for the formed parts. Bars spill spirits and wipe tables with alcohol or quaternary sanitiser. (4) Cement vapour: Core's two ball halves are 'joined at the equator' (PARTICULARS.md). Hemisphere's three formed layers are bonded at the rim around sealed gaps, vented only through a press-in ePTFE plug (crystal.py:223-225). Roehm's fault table, quoted in r46-owner-notes:spinoffs/barkhorn/research/2026-10-31/R8-fab-fallbacks.md:227, cures crazing by annealing after each bonding step; no lamp process has that step. NEEDED: one compatibility list for the line, covering lockers (use a nylon patch or a plastic-safe grade), oils, greases, cord jackets, foam and VHB tapes, cements, cleaners and bar sanitisers. Then apply Tropos's stressed, annealed coupon exposure test to the shade crown, the formed ball and the Mantle deck. Medium: the overhead shade is the route to injury; elsewhere it is crazing that can grow into cracks on show surfaces.

missing_across_line.topic: Transit, packaging and owner set-up: the shipping plan hands the owner the joints the reviews found weakest
missing_across_line.products: Tropos, Mantle, Core, Hemisphere, Mother desk globe
missing_across_line.why_it_matters: DOCUMENTED ONLY AS A CONCEPT: r47-brand:spinoffs/barkhorn/brandbook/PACKAGING.md proposes crates and ISTA 3A/3B tests ('every size, stock and test below is a proposal'). Mantle's crate is 'to be drawn', and the Mother desk globe has nothing. No first-article plan (r33-speaker-horn:spinoffs/barkhorn/make/fai.md; r32-lamps-final:spinoffs/barkhorn/companions/launch/first-articles.md) has a transit, drop or shock step. No owner manual or set-up sheet exists on any branch, though certification.md lists 'the markings and the manual' for the lab. NOT CHECKED BY ANYONE: what the packing plan does at set-up. (a) Tropos's horn travels in its own case, and the owner 'crowns' the cabinet with it. That means taking the twist-lock cap off, plugging the HF pair back in inside the pod (r33-speaker-horn:spinoffs/barkhorn/product.py:639, 'unplugged here, the horn lifts off its sockets'), and doing up the M6 rod's knurled thumb nut 'by hand' (product.py:1699-1700). The Tropos review's rocking threshold (15-31 N formed, 23-46 N Strata) depends on that rod's preload (0-1 kN). The checks that would catch a loose or reversed horn, FAI M4 ('cannot be lifted') and E2 (polarity), are factory steps the owner never repeats. (b) Mantle ships 'the platter, hub and spindle ... in its own foam, a nitrile cap on the housing' (r48-mantle-design:spinoffs/barkhorn/companions/mantle-r48/README.md:142); mantle_outcrop.py:414 says instead 'platter off, the spindle in'. Either way the owner makes the first insertion into the unvented bearing, which the Mantle review says takes 10 min to 75 h to seat. An owner who presses instead loads the 6 mm carbide ball once the oil escapes. With p0 proportional to F^(1/3), a 100 N push on top of the assembly's 20.3 N gives 2.32 x (120/20.3)^(1/3) = 4.2 GPa, ISO 76's static limit; 200 N gives about 5.1 GPa, enough to brinell the plate and add rumble. The r48 critic's 'nothing seals the oil for transit' and 'no transit locks or packaging' (critic/r1-baseline/cad-review.md:25,54) are still open for Strata v2. (c) The Mother desk globe has no packaging. It is about 0.34 m2 of 8 mm sheet, roughly 3.3 kg (my estimate), and its review found 22 of its 23 pieces held by cement alone. (d) Core balls are 'sold separately' (PARTICULARS.md) and ship alone by parcel. (e) Hemisphere's drum holds the shade only by its collar, so every transit shock passes through the clamped, thread-locked crown named in the item above.

missing_across_line.topic: Lithium transport mode for Core: four documents, two answers, and the 2026 air state-of-charge rule
missing_across_line.products: Core (sales, spare cells, returns and warranty shipments)
missing_across_line.why_it_matters: DOCUMENTED, AND CONTRADICTORY. r32-lamps-final:spinoffs/barkhorn/companions/launch/certification.md recommends shipping the three cells loose 'in the box beside the lamp (UN3481, packed with equipment)'. Its reason is a 2019 PHMSA letter that treats cells electrically connected through a circuit board as a 'battery', which needs its own UN 38.3 test. r46-owner-notes:spinoffs/barkhorn/research/2026-10-31/R3-compliance.md (section 1.4; section 3, Core step 7) says 'Ship Core with its cells installed'. r47-brand:spinoffs/barkhorn/brandbook/PACKAGING.md says 'The cells ship fitted in the base'. PARTICULARS.md and out-orb-table/bom.md say UN3481 'contained in equipment'. If the cells ship fitted, the files' own PHMSA reading calls for a pack-level UN 38.3 test (R3 estimates $5-15k), and no budget or schedule includes it. If they ship beside the lamp, every parcel needs the UN3481 lithium mark (R3, USPS PI 9D). Also, since 1 Jan 2026, IATA requires Li-ion cells above 2.7 Wh that are packed with equipment (PI 966) to travel at no more than 30 % state of charge. Core's cells are 4.8 Wh (carrier notices: https://www.jal.co.jp/jp/en/jalcargo/inter/news/20251229-01/ ; https://www.lion.com/lion-news/december-2025/new-lithium-battery-state-of-charge-limit-in-effect-jan-1 ; https://racklify.com/encyclopedia/lithium-battery-shipping/). LiFePO4's flat voltage curve means 30 % can't be set or checked by voltage; the lamps review found the same for fuel gauging. It has to be counted out, about 0.7 x 1.5 Ah = 1.05 Ah from full, yet the first-article runtime and charge tests leave the cells full. Any air leg is affected: express and priority services, Hawaii and Alaska. So is the returns path: r46-owner-notes:spinoffs/barkhorn/launch/policies-draft.md:117 says 'we send packaging and a prepaid label', and customers will send lamps back with the cells fitted. The energy figures also disagree. R3 uses 5.7 Wh a cell and 17 Wh in all; the BOM says 4.8 Wh and 14.4 Wh. R3's DOE limit, 0.1440 x 17 + 2.95 = 5.40 kWh/yr, becomes 5.02 at 14.4 Wh. This hurts no one. It decides whether Core can legally go by air and whether an unbudgeted test is needed.

missing_across_line.topic: ESD and EMC design inside acrylic bodies that give no shielding
missing_across_line.products: Core, Mantle, Tropos, Hemisphere, Mother desk globe
missing_across_line.why_it_matters: No review examined this. US law tests emissions only: an FCC Part 15B SDoC, which R3 notes must be done before anything is delivered (47 CFR 2.803). Acrylic gives no shielding, yet no product specifies filtering, cable ferrites, layout rules or ESD protection. Core's LTC4162 switching charger drives a 2 m USB-C cable. Mantle's 25 kHz PWM dimmer feeds a 1.2 m strip loop in the base under the deck that carries the MM phono stage. The first-article hum test covers only audio-band hum. Immunity: Core's touch electrode is the anodised ring that people tap and the ball sits in (r32-lamps-final:spinoffs/barkhorn/companions/crystal.py:402-404). An anodic film of 10-25 um breaks down well below the 8 kV of an IEC 61000-4-2 air discharge, and no series resistor or TVS is specified. The board has no schematic yet (launch/boards.md, per the lamps review). The Mother review called for a TVS on the desk globe's base touch; nobody did for Core. Mantle's arm, clamp and bearing housing tie to the star earth and the phono stage's input ground (r48-mantle-design out-strata-v2/bom.md, 'wiring'). The deck and lid around them, the r48 critic says, 'will build up a lot of static' (critic/r1-baseline/cad-review.md, item 10). None of this blocks US shipping. But these are the usual causes of a failed first FCC test and of field returns. Immunity also becomes mandatory under CE (EN 55035 for audio, EN 61547 for lighting) if the Vienna showing turns into EU sales (r47-brand:spinoffs/barkhorn/brandbook/facts/SEQUENCE.md:48: 'Shown there: the pair, Mantle, the lamps').
